figure: Table 20-1 — 'Aggregate rps' target and undefined 'per-query time'
issue: Two definitional weaknesses. (a) 'Aggregate rps' is defined as an observed quantity ('Total queries processed per second across all hosts') but its Target is a provisioning requirement ('>= 2x peak rps for comfort margin'), so the row mixes a measurement with a capacity decision; a reader could read it as a measured condition that the fleet must satisfy. (b) 'Scheduling overhead' is defined as 'Fraction of per-query time spent in dispatcher, not compute' with target '< 5%', but 'per-query time' is undefined (end-to-end? service time? queueing-inclusive?), and the two scheduler rows bind very differently: at the canonical 8.6 s service time, 5% is ~430 ms, far looser than the '< 100 ms' p99 row, so the table does not tell the reader which constraint governs.
evidence: Rendered table rows: 'Aggregate rps | Total queries processed per second across all hosts | >= 2x peak rps for comfort margin (stress/soak target — see note)'; 'Scheduling overhead | Fraction of per-query time spent in dispatcher, not compute | < 5%'; 'Scheduler-added p99 latency | 99th-percentile time a request waits in the fleet dispatcher (NOT end-to-end — model execution is multi-second here) | < 100 ms'.
acceptance_test: Rename the first row to make the metric a capacity figure (e.g. 'Provisioned aggregate rps' with definition 'aggregate capacity across all hosts') or restate the target as a threshold on the measured value; define 'per-query time' explicitly (e.g. 'end-to-end request latency'); and add a note stating which of the scheduler rows binds first at the canonical service time. Also verify that the 'see note' referenced in the first Target cell exists and is reachable from this page (NOT VERIFIED here — the note is not on this page).

issue: The table's first definition uses 'queries' ('Total queries processed per second across all hosts') while the same table's second row uses 'requests' ('time a request waits in the fleet dispatcher'), and the surrounding book consistently uses 'request' for the unit of work (e.g. 'per-request tokens', 'requests/second'). 'Query' is used elsewhere in the book for the agentic user input ('Take a user query routed to an agentic RQA pipeline'), so the two terms are not interchangeable in this book's own usage.

figure: FIGURE 20.1 — Fleet capacity vs host count (canonical workload)
issue: The figure's caption and its own Note assign different host counts to the same derate name. Caption: 'the throughput-efficiency derate flattens the canonical 40 rps peak once 22 hosts are provisioned — 21 ideal / 22 at 95% efficiency on the KV screen — 23 with the p95 derate on the case (ii) prefill screen (§3)'. Note: 'this figure models the KV-residency/throughput screen only (21 hosts ideal, 22 at p95; the prefill screen in §3 binds higher — 23 hosts (case (ii) with the p derate)...)'. The in-figure annotation agrees with the caption ('21 hosts (ideal / 22 at 95%)'), so the Note is the outlier: it labels the 0.95 throughput-efficiency factor as 'p95' while the caption reserves 'p95 derate' for a different, larger derate that yields 23 hosts. A reader who takes '22 at p95' literally gets 22 where the caption says 23.
evidence: Caption clause '22 at 95% efficiency on the KV screen — 23 with the p95 derate' vs Note clause '21 hosts ideal, 22 at p95' vs in-figure annotation '21 hosts (ideal / 22 at 95%)'. Independently re-derived: C_analytic(N)=N×17/8.6=1.9767 req/s/host; C_eff=0.95×C_analytic; C_eff=40 at N=21.30 (so 22 hosts at the 95% derate, 21 hosts ideal where C_analytic=40 at N=20.24). The 0.95 factor is the throughput-efficiency derate, not the p95 derate; the two are distinct quantities in the caption's own usage.
acceptance_test: In the source, the Note must read '21 hosts ideal, 22 at 95% efficiency' (or whatever single term the chapter uses for the 0.95 factor), and the p95 derate must be named only where it produces 23 hosts. After the edit, grep the figure caption, the Note, and the in-figure annotation for 'p95' / '95%' and confirm exactly one derate is called '95%' and the host counts 21 / 22 / 23 map one-to-one onto ideal / 95% / p95.

figure: Prose (Note 22.1-1 continuation), no figure on page
issue: The host-count arithmetic appears inconsistent as rendered: 'the canonical 10 rps average demand is 10 × 1.288 = 12.88 PFLOP/s ≈ 1.6 hosts at 100% of peak and ≈1.4 at 40% MFU (Ch 24 §3.3)'. Re-deriving with the book's canonical 8×H100 host: 12.88 PFLOP/s ÷ (8 × 0.989 PFLOP/s per H100 at FP16 dense) = 1.63 hosts at 100% of peak, which matches '≈1.6'. At 40% MFU the same demand needs 12.88 ÷ (8 × 0.989 × 0.40) = 4.07 hosts, i.e. ≈4.1, not 1.4. The rendered token may in fact be '4.1' misread at 150 dpi, in which case the sentence is correct; if it is '1.4', the sentence states that 40% MFU needs FEWER hosts than 100% of peak, which is impossible.
